D018-D019_h001.question_a:

I keep getting these images in my head of the moment it happened, like it’s replaying on a loop. It just pops in, even when I’m not trying to think about it, and it hits me hard. I feel on edge all the time, like something bad is about to happen again. There’s this constant tension in my body, almost like I’m bracing for impact.

Loud sounds in the station—someone dropping a toolbox, a train horn—make me jump out of my skin. I physically flinch. My head feels foggy most days; it’s hard to think straight or focus on the signals. I used to care a lot about doing well at work, maybe getting promoted, but now it’s like I don’t feel anything about that. I keep going over it in my mind, blaming the station staff and management for not having better barriers, like if they’d done their jobs right this wouldn’t have happened.

I don’t want to think about it, but it just pops in, like my brain is replaying it without asking me.

I catch myself replaying that call and blaming that mom, my coworkers, even the system, and I walk around simmering, snapping over nothing. It started about two weeks ago, after that accident on the highway when a car clipped my bike and I saw another rider get hit badly. Since then, I just don’t feel like myself.

Almost every night I have these really vivid nightmares about it. Sometimes it’s the exact scene, sometimes it’s different, but it’s always the same feeling—me on the road, something smashing into me, people screaming. I wake up sweating and my heart’s racing, and it takes a while to realize I’m in my room, not on the road.

During the day I’m constantly on edge. Even when I’m not riding, I feel this constant sense that something terrible is about to happen. I’m jumpy with every loud sound, and my body feels tense all the time.

I’ve also been snapping at people over nothing—customers, other riders, even my mom on the phone. It’s like I go from zero to furious in seconds, then feel stupid afterward.

What’s weird is, even when I hit my delivery targets or get good tips now, I don’t feel happy or proud. It all just feels flat, like nothing is really worth anything.
